title: Super chunky mittens
subtitle: Ultra-fast full mittens in super-chunky wool, knitted in the round.
excerpt: Full mittens in super-chunky wool, worked in the round in stocking stitch. Each mitt takes about 20 minutes at super-chunky gauge. Afterthought thumb. One size fits most adults.
sourceNotes: Super-chunky mittens worked in the round. Construction follows the standard seamless mitten structure scaled to 6 stitches per 10 cm at super-chunky gauge.

knitting.gaugeText: 8 sts x 12 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in stocking stitch on 10 mm needles.
knitting.finishedSizeText: One size: hand circumference approximately 20 to 23 cm.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Full mittens in super-chunky wool, worked in the round in stocking stitch with an
afterthought thumb
. One size fits most adults. Each mitt takes about 20 minutes at super-chunky gauge.
At 10 mm needles and super-chunky weight, the stitch count is very low and each round is fast. The construction uses
magic loop

on a long circular. Budget about 120 g (65 m / 70 yards) of super-chunky wool per pair. With super-chunky yarn the long-tail cast-on requires a very long tail: pull off at least 40 cm before starting.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 120 g (about 65 m / 70 yards) of super-chunky-weight wool

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 10 mm (UK 000 / US 15) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 3: 1 for beginning of round, 1 for thumb, 1 for top shaping midpoint

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 40 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the thumb

content.text: Gauge

8 stitches and 12 rounds to 10 cm in stocking stitch on 10 mm needles. The low stitch count means a 1-stitch gauge difference changes the finished circumference by about 2.5 cm; swatch before casting on.
Pattern
Cast on and cuff
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 16 stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 6 rounds of 2x2 rib.
Hand body
Switch to stocking stitch. Work 3 rounds. Place the thumb: work the first 4 stitches with waste yarn, slip back, and knit to end. Continue in stocking stitch for 6 more rounds.
Top shaping

Place a marker at the midpoint (between stitches 8 and 9). Decrease round: k1, ssk, k to 3 before midpoint, k2tog, k1, SM, k1, ssk, k to last 3, k2tog, k1. Plain round. Repeat until 4 stitches remain. Cut yarn and draw through all 4 stitches.
Thumb
Remove waste yarn. Pick up 4 stitches above and 4 stitches below the gap. Work 4 rounds of stocking stitch. Bind off.
Common faults
Tight cast-on edge: the long-tail cast-on at 10 mm pulls more than it does at smaller gauges. Cast on over two needles held together and remove one before joining to the round.
Top shaping closes too fast: the decrease round removes 4 stitches per pair of rounds; at 16 stitches this leaves only one or two pairs of decrease rounds before the final 4. Count carefully.
Finishing
Thread the tail through your tapestry needle and weave in on the wrong side.
Care
Hand wash in cool water with wool-safe detergent. Lay flat to dry. Super-chunky fabric takes longer to dry than standard DK.
What to try next
The chunky fingerless mitts use the same flat seamed construction at a slightly finer gauge. Going from super-chunky to chunky weight is a good way to practise gauge adjustment.
